biography.plain_text: Cuthbert Francis Dixon-Johnson was a British army officer and political writer associated with Croft-on-Tees in Yorkshire. He served in the 6th Dragoons and was promoted to captain in 1901. A son of iron merchant Cuthbert Greenwood Dixon-Johnson, he became an advocate of Ottoman interests and wrote about Britain’s Near Eastern policy.

long_biography.plain_text:
During the war between Italy and the Ottoman Empire, Cuthbert Francis Dixon-Johnson directed a British medical mission in Libya. Its team included surgeons Charles Edgar Holton Smith and Bernard Haigh. The mission worked through hospitals at Gharien and Yefren, with members travelling through the country by camel.

Dixon-Johnson also sought to influence public opinion through political pamphlets. In The Armenians, published in 1916, he defended Ottoman policy and dismissed accounts of mass killing as fabricated or exaggerated. He attacked British supporters of the Armenians and argued that Britain had damaged its interests by abandoning its former friendship with Turkey.
